# ECN-2026-022 - Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

## Reason for change
This engineering change notice documents a required update to the documented minimum coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01). Field verification and vendor guidance revealed that previous documentation and control setpoints allowed flows below the safe operating value for the heater coil cooling circuit. Operating at lower flow has repeatedly produced coil outlet temperatures and diagnostics that indicate elevated risk of localized overheating and accelerated insulation degradation. The change aligns operational controls and maintenance acceptance criteria with the verified minimum flow requirement to preserve coil life and to maintain safe and reliable heater performance.

Related guidance and background from recent change activity and procedures are recorded in ECN-2026-029 and in the operational procedures SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-04. This ECN updates machine-specific requirements only; procedural updates to operator checklists and SOPs are tracked in the related documents cited above.

Rationale:
- Remove ambiguity between machine wiring diagrams, the unit PLC interlocks, and the maintenance acceptance criteria.
- Reduce unplanned heater outages attributed to coil overheating and insulation faults.
- Standardize entry criteria for planned maintenance and for run-permit interlocks.

## Affected items
- Machine: Machining induction billet heater #1, equipment tag EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
- Operator checklists and pre-start verification items used on line P1-L3, referenced in SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-04.
- PLC analog input mapping and alarm thresholds that govern the coil cooling water flow permissive and associated inhibit logic.
- Maintenance acceptance criteria and torque verification steps that reference coil cooling performance.

Specific change to be recorded on equipment nameplate and in the equipment record: the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. This value is to be treated as the minimum allowable flow for normal operation and will be used for commissioning, acceptance, and alarm limits.

Examples of scenarios to which the change applies:
- During start-up, the cooling water flow reading must be verified against the minimum value prior to establishing heater drive enable.
- During preventative inspections, if measured flow is at or below the minimum, tagging and corrective action are required prior to return to service.
- When troubleshooting coil-related alarms, flow verification to this minimum is a first-line diagnostic step.

## Implementation
Scope:
- Update equipment record and drawing notes for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to include the specified minimum coil cooling water flow.
- Update PLC alarm and interlock thresholds associated with the flow permit so that a below-minimum condition generates a visible alarm and inhibits heater enable.
- Revise the pre-start checklist in SOP-P1-L3-01 and the maintenance acceptance checklist in SOP-P1-L3-04 to include explicit verification of the minimum flow value for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.

Actions and sequence:
1) Engineering will issue an updated equipment data sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 reflecting the required flow minimum and attach it to the equipment file.
2) Controls will change the flow permissive setpoint and the alarm setpoint in the PLC to reference the minimum. Controls will document the ladder or function block changes in the control change log.
3) Operations will receive a brief awareness briefing covering the revised pre-start checks and the location of the equipment nameplate stating the minimum flow.
4) Maintenance will incorporate the minimum flow verification into the standard maintenance checklist for coils and circulation systems. Records of measured flow will be retained as maintenance evidence.
5) Commissioning verification will demonstrate that with the revised interlock in place the heater will not enable when measured flow is below the minimum. Results will be recorded in the commissioning record.

Records to keep:
- Updated equipment data sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 with the minimum coil cooling water flow note.
- Controls change log entries showing the PLC modifications and justification.
- Commissioning test report demonstrating interlock functionality and alarm behavior.
- Operator pre-start checklist entries showing flow verification for an agreed number of consecutive starts following implementation.
- Maintenance inspection reports showing periodic verification of actual flow against the minimum value.

Examples of acceptable records entries:
- A maintenance report entry shall state the measurement method, the measured value, and confirmation that the measured flow meets or exceeds the minimum as referenced on the equipment data sheet.
- Controls log entries shall include the file and function block names revised, a brief rationale, and the signature of the responsible engineer.

Note on measurement method:
Use the method specified in SOP-P1-L3-04 for measuring coil cooling water flow and record instrument identification as part of the evidence. If temporary flow measurement equipment is used for verification, the instrument serial or tag used must be recorded in the maintenance report.

Change timing and coordination:
- Implementation requires coordination between Engineering, Controls, Operations, and Maintenance to schedule PLC updates and operator training without disrupting production continuity. Controls will coordinate an installation window with Operations.

## Approvals
- Engineering: approval required to update equipment data sheet and issue ECN.
- Controls: approval required for PLC interlock and alarm changes.
- Operations: acknowledgment of revised pre-start procedures and acceptance of training.
- Maintenance: acknowledgment of revised maintenance acceptance criteria and recordkeeping requirements.

Approvals shall be recorded in the ECN approval block and in the equipment file. Reference related documents ECN-2026-029, SOP-P1-L3-01, and SOP-P1-L3-04 for procedural detail and for any follow-up tasks that propagate to standardized procedures.
